title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page from the 'Teichmülleries' notes of 1981-83, the period that leads to the Teichmüller-tower sections of the Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The page has three parts.

(0) Struck-out first line. It computes the conjugate rho~^3(tau~'_inf) = omega~_0^{-1} tau~'_inf omega~_0 and rewrites it via omega~_0^{-1} tau~_inf omega~_0 tau~'^{-1}_inf tau~'_inf = omega~_0^{-2} tau~'_0 = ... This is a relation check in a lifted (tilde) group, probably a central or braid-type extension of a genus-0 or genus-1 modular group with generators attached to the cusps 0, 1, infinity. He abandoned it.

(1) Generators for the type-(1,2) group. He lists five elements: tau'', tau, eps_0, eps_1, eps_2. A plausible reading:
- eps_0, eps_1, eps_2 are Dehn twists ('cylinders') on the twice-marked torus.
- tau'' is an orientation-reversing involution (complex conjugation), so the groups are the extended ones, containing GL(2,Z) rather than SL(2,Z).
- tau is the element exchanging the two marked points.

His claims:
- <tau'', eps_0, eps_1> = GL(2,Z), a copy of the extended group of the once-marked torus.
- <tau'', eps_2, eps_1^{-1}> = GL(2,Z), a second copy.
- <tau'', eps_1> = D_{eps_1}, an infinite dihedral group: a reflection inverting a twist.
- tau permutes the two GL(2,Z) copies and acts on D_{eps_1}.

From this he proposes, with both '!' and '?' over the sign, T_{1,2} ≅ GL(2,Z) *_{D_inf} GL(2,Z), perhaps up to the extension by tau. The aim is a 'lego' description of the genus-1, two-point Teichmüller group by amalgamating the genus-1, one-point pieces along the stabiliser of a common cylinder. This is the program of Esquisse §§2-3: build the tower from modular dimension ≤ 2.

(2) A sketch of a sphere with several arcs from the top (poles/meridians). The text describes a configuration of 3g cylinders (simple closed curves) on a genus-g surface. Any two of them are either disjoint or in 'standard position'. Standard position is described in his globe language: two parallel cylinders, i.e. poles, or a polar cylinder and a transverse one relative to an equatorial axis, i.e. meeting once. He counts the meeting pairs: 2g + 2·g(g-1)/2 = 2g(1+(g-1)/2) = g(g+1) pairs are in standard position, and all other pairs are disjoint. This looks like a search for a combinatorial generating system of Dehn twists for the genus-g group, with prescribed pairwise braid or commutation relations, in the spirit of Lickorish (3g-1 twists) and Humphries (2g+1).
errors:
The conjectured isomorphism T_{1,2} ≅ GL(2,Z) *_{D_inf} GL(2,Z) cannot hold if T_{1,2} is the (extended, pure or full) mapping class group of the torus with two marked points: the rational Euler characteristics disagree.
- Amalgam: chi(GL2Z) + chi(GL2Z) - chi(D_inf) = -1/24 - 1/24 - 0 = -1/12.
- Orientation-preserving pure group: Harer–Zagier gives chi(Gamma_1^2) = (2-2-1)·chi(Gamma_1^1) = (-1)(-1/12) = +1/12. Hence +1/24 for the extended group and +1/48 with the point exchange.
- The orientation-preserving analogue SL2Z *_Z SL2Z (chi = -1/6) also fails.
So at best the natural map from the amalgam is not injective (it is surjective if the stated generation holds); the '?' was justified. (The abelianisation Z/12 is consistent with the amalgam, so only a finer invariant like chi detects the failure.)
The first line is struck out by Grothendieck himself; its final equality omega~_0^{-2} tau~'_0 = ... is incomplete.
The count 2g + 2·g(g-1)/2 = g(g+1) is arithmetically correct. The intermediate '= 2g(1+(g-1)/2)' is fine, but the bracket is never closed on the page.

ideas.what: The extended mapping class group of the once-marked torus as GL(2,Z), generated by two twists and a reflection; the stabiliser of a cylinder as an infinite dihedral group
ideas.modern_name: Mod^±(S_{1,1}) ≅ GL(2,Z); stabiliser of a curve in the extended group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses T_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) informally

ideas.what: Conjectural presentation of the genus-1, two-point Teichmüller group as an amalgam of two genus-1, one-point groups over a dihedral cylinder stabiliser, with the point exchange tau swapping the factors
ideas.modern_name: amalgam / complex-of-groups decomposition of Mod(S_{1,2}); 'lego' of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's lego idea (Esquisse); presentations of Mod(S_{1,2}) via Gervais, Wajnryb; tower presentations by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 describes the lego in general terms but not this amalgam formula as far as I know

ideas.what: A system of 3g simple closed curves on a genus-g surface, pairwise disjoint or meeting once, with exactly g(g+1) meeting pairs; probably intended as a Dehn-twist generating set
ideas.modern_name: Dehn twist generating systems / intersection graphs (Lickorish, Humphries chains)

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectured an amalgam decomposition of the genus-1, two-point Teichmüller group into two GL(2,Z)'s over an infinite dihedral group. An Euler-characteristic count shows this is false for Mod^±(S_{1,2}). Whether he meant a different group, or the correct statement is a graph/complex of groups with more vertices, is left open on the page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical witness of Grothendieck testing a concrete 'lego' gluing for T_{1,2}. Its failure illustrates why the Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps style presentations need the pentagon/2-dimensional relations rather than a mere tree of groups. This is of minor interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: Scratch work on generators of the (1,2) Teichmüller group with a tentative amalgam formula, which appears false by an Euler-characteristic count, plus a curve-configuration count. It is a nice glimpse of the 'lego' program in action but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'opère[?] sur D_{ε1}' reads as 'et opère sur D_{ε1}'; the margin text is 'τ permute ces deux sous-groupes Gl(2,Z) et opère sur D_{ε1}'.
Below the arrow, the amalgamating subgroup is written D_∞, matching D_{ε1} above.

The superscripts '4' and '5' in the last lines are not footnotes. They belong to the overlaid typed label ('MR LE PROFESSEUR GROTHENDIECK ALEX. / MATHEMATIQUES'); the handwritten text reads 'paires de cylindres en position standard, et les autres paires sont disjointes'.
Archive page number in the corner is 154.
